scope: Proposition 5.6 (Higgs tails) of the manuscript “The reverse logarithmic Kodaira inequality and additivity” (preprints/The-reverse-logarithmic-Kodaira-inequality-and-additivity-September-26-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 033 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 499df173e9f8ba2d), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 34. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let h : W → S be any dominant morphism of smooth connected projective varieties with connected generic fiber. On a dense algebraic open of W, suppose that ℓ ⊂ h∗E0 is an algebraic line subbundle. Require that the pointwise instability-parabolic construction of Theorem 4.5, applied to ℓ, gives exactly the pulled-back compact marks h∗ju. This compatibility is part of the hypothesis. Take a smooth connected unipotent level π : c W → W dominating the level used to define H, and resolve its boundary and the generated subspace maps. Over the variation locus, let Gi be the span of all contractions of θi(ℓ) in π∗h∗ Grp∗−i F A, with G0 = ℓ. Use the resulting subbundles of the extended Hodge grades on c W. Put Uj = M i≥j Gi, P = − X j≥0 det Uj = − X i≥0 (i + 1) det Gi. (5.11) Only finitely many summands are nonzero. Then P is nef and ν P + π∗ h∗ H  = ν(P). (5.12) The assertion applies to every such h and every such compatible line; ℓ need not be the original vector used to construct S.
